uncited: It sets itself apart from the [Contour Tree](9312-contour-tree.md) by explicitly handling genus (loops) in the input domain, and from the [Joint Contour Net](9316-joint-contour-net.md) by operating on single-variable scalar fields rather than multivariate data.
The Reeb graph is constructed by analyzing the connectivity of level sets of a scalar function $f: M \to \mathbb{R}$ defined on a domain $M$.
The algorithm typically operates on a discretized representation of the domain.
The mesh consists of vertices, edges, and triangles (or higher-dimensional simplices).
The implementation relies on the simplicial mesh structure.
The graph itself is typically stored as an adjacency list or a merge/join tree structure that is subsequently modified to handle loops.
*   As the sweep line (or plane/hyperplane) moves, it updates the connectivity of the level sets.
*   Let $f: M \to \mathbb{R}$ be the scalar function.
*   **When to use:** Use when the scalar field is defined on a domain with loops (e.g., torus) or no boundary, and single-variable topology is sufficient.
Use when online/streaming computation is required.
*   **When not to use:** Use the [Contour Tree](9312-contour-tree.md) if the domain is simply connected and boundary exists, as it is simpler.
Use [Joint Contour Net](9316-joint-contour-net.md) or [Multi-Dimensional Reeb Graph](9382-multi-dimensional-reeb-graph.md) if the data is multivariate.
